cards.raw0:
Which substance is generated in response to PNS innervation via the pelvic nerve to mediate an erection?

{{c1::Nitric oxide (NO), which causes increased cGMP}}
cards.back: - ACh from the greater and lesser cavernosal nerves stimulates vascular endothelium to increase intracellular Ca 2+ , which activates NO synthase (converts L-arginine to NO) - This causes trabecular smooth muscle in the helicine arterioles to relax, allowing vasodilation (expansion of corpora cavernosa / corpus spongiosum), blood accumulates and compresses venules against tunica albuginea (blocks venous outflow resulting in tumescence ) [img] Photo credit: Mcstrother , CC BY 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Which substance is released by the SNS to inhibit an erection ( detumescence )? [Norepinephrine]
cards.raw0:
Which substance is released by the SNS to inhibit an erection (detumescence)?

{{c1::Norepinephrine}}
cards.back: - Norepinephrine increases calcium in trabecular smooth muscle, resulting in helicine arterioles vasoconstriction and allowing drainage of excess blood - Norepinephrine = ↑ [Ca 2+ ] → contraction of smooth muscles → VC → anti-erectile [img] Photo credit: Mcstrother , CC BY 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.raw0: Anovulatory cycles lead to the breakdown and shedding of proliferative glands resulting in abnormal {{c1::uterine bleeding}}

cards.front: [Linkage disequilibrium] describes the tendency of alleles at two loci on the same chromosome to be inherited together more or less often than expected by chance
cards.raw0: {{c1::Linkage disequilibrium}} describes the tendency of alleles at two loci on the same chromosome to be inherited together more or less often than expected by chance
cards.back: - Linkage is the tendency of alleles at two loci to be inherited together (often due to physical proximity of genes on a chromosome, but disequilibrium does not always imply physical linkage) - The further apart loci are, the more likely a break will be introduced during replication and allow for a recombination event to generate a non-parental (recombinant) allele - The closer together loci are, the less likely a recombination event is to occur (as recombination frequency goes from 0.5 to 0, linkage disequilibrium increases)

cards.front: Linkage disequilibrium is measured in a(n) [population], not in a family
cards.raw0: Linkage disequilibrium is measured in a(n) {{c1::population}}, not in a family
cards.back: - Often varies in different populations - The closer two loci are, the less likely there is a recombination event; thus, the amount of people needed to see a recombination event would be unfeasible to do in even the largest families

cards.front: If alleles at two loci are inherited equally as expected by chance, the loci are said to be in [linkage equilibrium ]
cards.raw0: If alleles at two loci are inherited equally as expected by chance, the loci are said to be in {{c1::linkage equilibrium}}
cards.back: When alleles at two loci are inherited more/less than expected by chance, the haplotype is said to be in linkage disequilibrium

cards.raw0: Cystic fibrosis may cause {{c1::infertility}} in men due to congenital bilateral absence of the {{c2::vas deferens}}
cards.back: - 95% of males with CF are infertile; CFTR mutations are likely responsible for abnormal development of wolffian structures, resulting in vasal agenesis and defective sperm transport - Spermatogenesis may be unaffected, thus can have children with assisted techniques [img] Photo credit: OpenStax , CC BY 4.0 [img] [img]
